subject.title: fix(approvals): fail closed plugin tool gates

question: Should legacy plugin `timeoutBehavior: "allow"` stop granting execution authority in this release train?
rationale: The strict authorization invariant is security-positive, but disabling a previously documented plugin fallback can stop existing plugin workflows and requires explicit ownership of the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Accept fail-closed cutover
options.body: Keep the field accepted but ignored, correct terminal classifications, document the transition, and require upgrade plus live runtime proof.

options.title: Stage compatibility
options.body: Preserve allow-on-timeout for a defined transition window and remove its authority only after explicit migration guidance.

options.title: Hold the stacked change
options.body: Pause this draft until the durable approvals stack is ready for one complete security and compatibility decision.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed cutover
recommendation.body: Keep the field accepted but ignored, correct terminal classifications, document the transition, and require upgrade plus live runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged approval transaction work and the current stacked approval series make this person the strongest available owner for the security and compatibility cutover.
